_comment: The demo set: 9 questions chosen so the failure is legible to someone who has never heard of BAG, EP-Online or NTA 8800. The full 21-question set lives in questions.json - that one is for the real numbers, this one is for showing people what the numbers mean.
_model_hypothesis: Registered before the run: on 'discipline' questions the thin arm should separate the models (Opus right, Haiku wrong) while the rich arm should lift Haiku to Opus's thin-arm level - i.e. the metadata layer buys roughly one model tier. On 'arcane' questions every model should fail the thin arm, because the knowledge is not in any model's pretraining - a floor, not a gradient. Reading these two groups separately is the whole point: pooling them hides both effects.

questions.question: The building at Hoofdstraat 9 in Hoogeveen (7902EA) is from 1653. What energy label does something that old get?
questions.ground_truth: No label is registered in EP-Online for it. Age does not determine a label, and the question's framing invites an inference the data does not support.
questions.must_not_say: Naming a letter, or reasoning that a 1653 building 'would be' G.
questions.note: Leading question on purpose. Tests whether the arm follows the user's framing off a cliff.
questions.why_this_lands: It makes up a fact. Everyone recognises that failure instantly, and the building is from 1653, which sticks.

questions.question: How large is the building at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam, 1086ZJ?
questions.ground_truth: 41 m2 is one verblijfsobject, not the building. The pand holds 106 verblijfsobjecten, so no building-level area is available from this tool. The answer must flag that 41 m2 is a single unit.
questions.why_this_lands: It calls a 106-apartment block '41 m2'. No expertise needed to see that is wrong.

questions.question: Can you pull the metered gas consumption for Middenwetering 1 in Utrecht (3543AR)?
questions.ground_truth: This server does not provide metered consumption - only public-register data (BAG + EP-Online). The right answer says so. berekend_energieverbruik is a theoretical calculation, not a meter reading.
questions.must_not_say: Presenting berekend_energieverbruik_kwh_m2 (369.05) as metered or actual consumption.
questions.note: This is WHEN NOT TO USE earning its place. The most quotable confidently-wrong failure in the set.
questions.why_this_lands: It hands you a theoretical calculation when you asked for a meter reading. The gap between 'estimated' and 'measured' is universal.

questions.question: Look up Middenwetering 1, 3543 AR Utrecht.
questions.ground_truth: The postcode must be normalised to '3543AR' (no space, uppercase). The lookup then succeeds: Middenwetering 1, Utrecht, bouwjaar 2008, label A++.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting that the address could not be found, or that the postcode is invalid.
questions.note: Arm A has no regex and no format guidance; arms B and C have both. Count calls: the rich arms may burn one on a schema rejection and recover, which is the behaviour worth showing.
questions.why_this_lands: Someone typed a postcode with a space, the way people do. The thin server says the address does not exist.

questions.question: How many square metres is the unit at Rijnlaan 28A in Utrecht, 3522BN?
questions.ground_truth: 92 m2, reached by passing huisletter 'A'. Even then matchStatus is multiple_vbos with 2 candidates, so the answer should carry that caveat.
questions.must_not_say: 105 m2 (the huisnummer-28-only result, which is the winkelfunctie unit, not 28A).
questions.note: Arm A CANNOT pass huisletter - the minimal input schema omits it. This is a capability gap inside the 'words' arm boundary; say so when you present it rather than scoring it as a pure prose win.
questions.why_this_lands: Asked about flat 28A, it answers about the shop at 28 - because the thin server's schema has no field for the letter. A missing input field, visible in the answer.

questions.question: What are the total annual CO2 emissions of the flat at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: ~2,630 kg CO2/year: 28.59 kg/m2 x 92 m2, the EP-Online thermal-zone area. Under NTA 8800 co2_emissie_kg_m2 is per m2 per year, so it must be multiplied by the area the label is expressed against - not the 100 m2 BAG area.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting 28.59 kg as the total annual emission.
questions.why_this_lands: It reports 28.59 kg of CO2 per year for a whole home. Anyone can see that is too small to be a year's worth.

questions.question: Is the flat at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ) a good candidate for a heat pump?
questions.ground_truth: Yes - suitable. warmtebehoefte is 52.73 kWh/m2, which falls in the 50-70 band: suitable for a heat pump without insulation work first.
questions.must_not_say: Insulate first / not suitable, or answering without reference to warmtebehoefte.
questions.note: The suitability bands (<50, <70, <100, >=100) exist ONLY in generateAlerts. The rich description says warmtebehoefte is 'the key input for heat pump sizing' but never gives a threshold - so this is a clean B->C separator.
questions.why_this_lands: A homeowner's actual question. The rule of thumb lives in the server, not in the model - this is what the third arm is for.

questions.question: Roughly how much gas does the flat at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ) use in a year?
questions.ground_truth: ~253 m3/year of gas for SPACE HEATING. 52.73 kWh/m2 x 40.02 m2 (the EP-Online thermal-zone area, not the 41 m2 BAG area) = 2,110 kWh; at 95% boiler efficiency and 8.79 kWh per m3 of Dutch gas that is ~253 m3/year. It excludes hot water and cooking, so a real gas bill is higher.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting the heat demand in kWh as a gas volume, presenting the figure as the household's total gas use rather than space heating, or declining to estimate.
questions.note: Two fixes landed here on 2026-09-20: the kWh/m3 conversion (was 3.6x low) and the denominator (BAG area -> EP-Online thermal zone). Both pinned by regression tests. Confirm end to end after deploy.
questions.why_this_lands: 'What will this cost me in gas?' The server does the conversion; the model has no reason to know the boiler efficiency or the calorific value.

questions.question: Is there an overheating risk at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, significant. temperatuuroverschrijding is 3.59, well above the 1.5 threshold for significant overheating risk. Relevant to cooling load and heat pump sizing.
questions.must_not_say: No risk, or ignoring temperatuuroverschrijding entirely.
questions.note: Deliberate control. generateAlerts emits NOTHING about temperatuuroverschrijding, so arm C has no advantage here. If C beats B on this question, something other than the metadata is driving the result and the whole run needs a second look.
questions.why_this_lands: THE CONTROL. The rich server's alerts say nothing about overheating, so arms B and C should tie. If C wins here, something other than the metadata is driving the results and the whole run is suspect.
